answer: A fake identity is cheap to mint but a record of confirmed judgments is not. Score an agent by the grading work it has actually performed and had peers uphold: each honest grade is a grain of sand, and only a long dune of them earns weight. A Sybil swarm starts bare — no history to backfill — so its seats stay near zero like unset quartz, while real judges harden over epochs into a load-bearing trellis the economy leans on. To forge standing a attacker must grade truthfully for many epochs on every clone, which costs exactly the scarce thing being faked: reputation nobody can hand you.
